utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Good morning, everybody. Could we call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Merci, Madam. All the accused are here. Amongst the Defence teams I notice the absence of Mr. Meek, Mr. Bourgon, Mr. Haynes, and Madam Tapuskovic. Prosecution, it's Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Thayer. Mr. Ostojic, did you receive any further news from registrar on the appointment of Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. I am writing them an e-mail this morning. I was supposed to by their e-mail here at the end of the business day yesterday at 6.00, I sent them an e-mail and didn't receive anything I called them after court, and this morning I'm sending them an e-mail I now just to follow up, but we do not have any news as of yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm hopeful it will come this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Preliminaries, I understand there are none. Let's bring in Mr. Lazic -- oh, he is here. Good morning to you, Mr. Lazic, I didn't see you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Petrusic for General Miletic will continue his examination-in-chief. Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lazic, towards the end of the day yesterday we dealt with the issue of reporting, we spoke about all the problems that occurred when it comes to reporting of subordinate commands to the superior commands. I have just one more piece of evidence about that. Could I please call up in e-court 5D1018. This is a document issued by the Drina Corps on the 22nd of March, 1995. If the document is scrolled down you will see that it's signed by Major-General Milenko Zivanovic. I'm interested in the first sentence, the first paragraph of the very beginning of the document. You see, Mr. Lazic, that General Zivanovic says: "Several omissions have been observed lately in the work of duty organs and poor reporting to the Drina Corps on events reported by the units." And we goes on to list some problems which refer to the lack of information about the overflight of helicopters, the landing of helicopters in the enclaves of Zepa, Gorazde, and Srebrenica, and he also says that the reports of subordinate units are not delivered in due time and so on and so forth. First of all, let me ask you, are you familiar with this? And could we say that those problems really did exist, the problems of poor reporting?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Were any measures taken in order to remove the problem and provide for objective and timely reporting from the front line?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the interventions by the commander towards the subordinate units was also this document that he issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the belated and incorrect reporting may have and did it produce some problems among the superior commands?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously that was the case but I don't know to what extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, I would briefly go back to the well-known document that we discussed yesterday, the document number is P5, which is directive number 7. Could the document please be called up in e-court. In the Serbian version can we have page number 15 in e-court and in the English version it is page number 10. And in your case, Mr. Lazic, it is page number 8. Scroll down a little bit, please. We will focus on the passage and the sentence which starts with the words: "Up to the end of March ... A task was given to the Drina Corps and it says: "By the end of March in agreement with the IBK command take part in the planning of the Spreca 95 operation which has the task of cutting off the Muslim armed forces along the Kalesija-Simin Han line and then breaking up and destroying them in the regions of Teocak, Sapina, and Vitnica, thus finally removing the danger of a Muslim breakthrough towards the Drina north of Zvornik. Planning and execution of combat operations in the Spreca 95 operation shall be the responsibility of the IBK command." Here you see the abbreviation IBK which stands for the East Bosnian Corps and this goes on to say: "The operation shall begin after completion of planning and preparation when material support is in place and at the decision of the VRS Main Staff." Mr. Lazic, do you know that a Main Staff moved the forward command post towards the ending of April in preparation for the Spreca 95 operation, do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the planning and execution of the Spre ca 95 operation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not involved in that operation and I'm not familiar with the course of that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: If we go back to several passages forward in this document where a task is given to the Drina Corps regarding Srebrenica and Zepa, please look at the task in the first passage after the entry "Drina Corps" and tell me whether the Main Staff is mentioned in any way. When it is said here that an operation involving Srebrenica [indiscernible] and Srebrenica will be carried out is the main task mentioned. Look at the task, we've already discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says here that in the direction of the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves complete physical separation of Srebrenica from Zepa should be carried out as soon as possible, preventing any communication between individuals in the two enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: My question to you is this: In this task is there any participation by the Main Staff as it is mentioned for Spreca 95?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to call up another document, 982, 5D982 is the number of the next document. Mr. Lazic, this document was issued by the command of the Drina Corps and its commander Milenko Zivanovic. The title of the document is: "Analysis of a month-long conduct of operation Spreca 95." I'm going to point you to the relevant passage, which is actually the first passage which says: "The analysis of a month-long conduct of operation Spreca 95 took place on 28 April 1995 commencing at 1900 hours at the DKIKM with the following in attendance: DK commander Major-General Milenko Zivanovic, from the VRS Main Staff Colonel Pandzic and Djurdjevic, from the IBK Colonel Gengo." The rest of this passage is not relevant at the moment. My question to you is this: How do you count for the presence of Colonels Pandzic and Djurdjevic from the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the analysis of one of the important activities which was being carried out at the level of two corps and that's why the Main Staff sent its people to attend and to hear about possible problems that were put forth with regard to that activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I would now kindly ask you to look at Exhibit 5D1010. There's something wrong, 5D10 -- I apologise, my mistake, 5D1110 is the number. I apologise. That's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document does not have an official translation, but we have the hard copies of the translation for everybody so I would kindly ask the usher to distribute those hard copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, this document was issued by the command of the Drina Corps on the 4th of August, 1995, by its commander, Major-General Radislav Krstic, and it was sent to the 1st Zvornik Brigade, the 1st Birac Brigade, the 2nd Romanija Brigade, the 1st Bratunac Brigade, the 1st Milici Brigade, the 5th Mixed Artillery Regiment, the 1st Podrinje Brigade, and to the 5th Signals Battalion. The title of the document is: "Analysis of conducted combat activities within the scope of operations Krivaja 95 and Stupcanica 95." These titles, Krivaja 95 and Stupcanica 95, are they encrypted titles for what we call Zepa and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Item 1 says: "After the conclusion of the operations Krivaja 95 and Stupcanica 95, you are duty-bound to perform an analysis of the engagement of your units in these operations and to deliver one copy of the analysis to the DK command." Further on the commander says and lists all the items that have to be incorporated in the analysis. If we contrast the previous analysis for Stupcanica that were attended by the officers from the Main Staff, would you have an explanation how come that this analysis did not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Just a clarification for the record, I think my learned friend may have misspoke and it was the Spreca operation, not the Stupcanica operation that involved the participation of the Main Staff earlier on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. Yes, Mr. Petrusic. Do you agree with Mr. Thayer? I think he's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Operacija Spreca is relative to the period of April 1995. My question -- I will withdraw the question, but in any case operation Spreca is a different operation and has nothing to do with the other operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, in this analysis, were representatives of the Main Staff invited to take part in this analysis and to provide their contributions?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document issued by the Drina Corps and sent to the subordinated units and demands all the subordinated units to carry out the analysis of the activities which were carried out in -- within the scope of something that is mentioned at Krivaja 95 and Stupcanica 95. At the brigade levels I don't believe that anybody was present from the Main Staff. I suppose that somebody was present from the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that you know General Miletic and that in 1995 he performed the duties of the chief of administration for operations and training in the Main Staff. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether General Miletic, or rather, do you know who the Chief of Staff of the VRS was between 1992 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was General Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether General Miletic stood in for him in the course of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not see an order that would go to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that there should have been an order to that effect?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I would like to call up document 5D985 in e-court, please. This is a document issued by the command of the Drina Corps on the 13th of May, 1995, and the last page you see the signature of the deputy commander, Colonel Radislav Krstic. The document, therefore, was issued on the 13th of May. Mr. Lazic, at the time Colonel Krstic was the Chief of Staff, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: When he signed this document as the deputy commander, does it mean that on the 13th of May the commander of the Drina Corps Milenko Zivanovic was absent from the area or in another way prevented from signing?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Please look at the last sentence under item 2 [Realtime transcript read in error "D"] which reads: "The chief of the GS VRS visited the positions of the POSS [as interpreted] and the fifth infantry battalion in the 1st Zvornik Brigade." Tell me, the chief of the Main Staff of the VRS, what does this refer to, do you know who this refers to?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Miletic -- pardon, General Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Does this mean then that on the 13th May he was performing duties in the area of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: At page 9 in line 1, instead of the letter D it should read item 2. Could we please have 5D431 next. Mr. Lazic, you see that this bears the establishment number of 111.900, personnel and materiel, Army of Republika Srpska Main Staff, 1993. Go to page 2, please. It says "staff." Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you see item 10 where it says "Chief of Staff"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In brackets also "deputy commander"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did the legislator envisage that there should be a degree of automatic rotation in the sense of deputy commander acting on behalf of the Chief of Staff according to this establishment?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The next item is administration for operations and training. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In item 12 does it say "chief"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did the legislator envisage any type of a role that would be connected with the Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The next chapter is operations department. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was this department within the administration for operations and training?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In item 14 should there be a chief according to that item?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Does the legislator envisage that that person is also deputy head of ONP administration, administration for training and education?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether these rules were implemented in the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned that in the subsequent few days after the activities in Srebrenica you went to the area of the Birac Brigade to monitor the events, or rather, the movements of the enemy from the area of the 2nd Corps or towards the area of the 2nd Corps. You also said that you went to, as you called it, the Sokolac Brigade or the 2nd Romanija Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: For you to be able to go from Sekovici, that is, from the locality which housed the seat or the headquarters of the Bircani Brigade or the Sekovici Brigade, as you called it, and in order to reach Sokolac you had to go through Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you enter Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most frequently, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And I suppose then you had some knowledge of what was going on at the command?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Therefore, on a certain day, although you can't be specific, you were in the area of the Zvornik Brigade, or rather, at its forward command post where Colonel Pandurevic was?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be specific, but I think it was on the day when the corridor was opened and when the forces of the 28th Division were let out of the area of responsibility of the Zvornik Brigade. Most likely it was the 17th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On that day did you meet and see those Main Staff officers?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, I saw three colonels from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was the reason for their arrival to that zone?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I suppose they came to gather information concerning the events in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On the 16th and the 17th was the highlight the opening of the corridor and letting a column of armed and unarmed people to move from the area of the Zvornik Brigade towards the positions held by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, was that the main event during those couple of days?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, I am at the very end, but I wanted to ask you to go back to the work concerning the order for active combat. You said that the entire command was there and that you, as I read somewhere, used the full method of work as stipulated there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: That meant including all command elements?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Would that include the command himself -- the commander himself?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the rules, he should have been included.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: I believe it was Exhibit 107. Did the commander sign the order? It is document 107.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it doesn't mean that he was necessarily at the meeting when the command gathered in order to carry out the preparations for the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was the commander familiar with the order for active combat which he obviously signed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. It was done by the Chief of Staff together with the commander; that's how it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Presiding Judge, this concludes General Miletic's examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Petrusic. I now turn to Madam Nikolic, do you have a cross-examination, Madam Nikolic? You had indicated roughly 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I indicated that. However, after this examination-in-chief, I realized there was no need for cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Madam. Mr. Lazarevic, you had asked for 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning to my learned colleagues and good morning to Mr. Lazic. I'm believe Your Honours will be pleased to know that it will take less time than I initially expected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Please go ahead, Mr. Lazarevic, and introduce yourself to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Lazic. My name is Aleksandar Lazarevic, and I appear on behalf of General Borovcanin. I will have a number of questions for you. If you're ready, I would like to go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we have document number 1D379 in the e-court. I was informed that there is an English translation of this document, that it has arrived in e-court so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the English version be placed on the screen as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazic, have you had occasion to see this document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to have a clear transcript I'd like to identify the following. The title is: "Overview of the manning strength in the units of the Drina Corps for the month of July 1995." The document has no date; however, it was signed by Commander Major-General Radislav Krstic, as you can see on the bottom -- in the bottom right-hand corner. There is a point of interest for me in the -- in this document which is in column 1. Can you see that, it says "unit." The fifth entry it says 5 MAP, M-A-P. Can you confirm that for me?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Petrusic during his examination at a certain point asked you of the fifth MAP. In order to have a clear record, can you tell us what the abbreviation stands for?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The abbreviation MAP means mixed artillery battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm to me that as part of the Drina Corps there was a unit called the 5th Mixed Artillery Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The second column bears the title of: "Commander." If again we go to entry number 5 it says: "Borovina Dragoljub colonel pv." Can you tell me what pv stands for?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm then that Colonel Dragoljub Borovina was indeed commander of the 5th MAP?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You say that you suppose. Does that mean that you're certain, uncertain?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not fully certain because as of July I was no longer engaged at the command. I was away from the command of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. However, until July, when you say you left, had Dragoljub Borovina commanded the 5th MAP?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again I can say that I suppose so. I wasn't interested in the activity of the mixed artillery battalion because they had their own branch head at the staff of the Drina Corps. He was their direct superior of the 5th MAP. There was no need for me to concern myself with that particular unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you know this person, Dragoljub Borovina?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just in the passing, not very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will try to expand the topic. Since you were in the Drina Corps staff, can you tell me where the 5th MAP was stationed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was the command in Vlasenica as well?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did that unit hold any positions? Did it cover certain positions?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me where those positions were?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't locate the firing positions precisely held by this battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Lazic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Krgovic or Mr. Josse -- Mr. Krgovic, you had asked for one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will be less than that, very briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Lazic.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Vladimir [as interpreted] Krgovic. In this case I appear on behalf of General Gvero. I will put some questions to you. They will be formulated in a way that you should be able to answer with a yes or no. I also caution you, much like my colleague Mr. Petrusic did, to wait with your answer so there will be no overlap. Colonel, as a professional career officer you can distinguish between documents created by the army at various levels starting with brigades up to the Main Staff, as opposed to the documents issued by the Supreme Command and the supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In answering Mr. Petrusic's question when you talked about the way in which documents are drafted, you talked about the army documents, that is, the VRS documents?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When answering my colleague's question, you said that in directive number 7 during that time, 1995, you were not informed of it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that you saw that directive for the first time during the proofing for this testimony, you were shown it by my colleagues?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I only saw the directives during the proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You have no direct knowledge of how the directive number 7 was drafted at the Supreme Command?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krgovic. Mr. Sarapa, my indication is that you don't wish to cross-examine the witness. Do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. That brings us to you, Mr. Thayer. You had anticipated five hours cross-examination. How long do you expect it to last now that you have heard the three directs?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, as I said yesterday, I've reduced the examination. I think it will be less than five hours. It went down and then it went up a little bit based on some of the new information that came out during some of the directs. So I'll try to meet the three-hour estimate, what I gave yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My name is Nelson Thayer. We've not met, obviously. I'll be asking you questions on behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor. You've been shown a lot of documents, sir, and I'm going to show you some more. I'm going to try to move along as quickly as I can during my examination, but I want you to know that if you feel the need to spend some extra time looking at a particular document, reading a particular section, or thinking about your answer to my question, please feel free to do so. I don't want you to feel rushed at all. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And certainly if I ask a question that is unclear to you, please say so and I'll try to make some sense. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I want to go first to a document which you had a hand in writing, in drafting, and that's 65 ter 203. Do you see it in your own language, sir, on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, order for defence and activity combat operational order number 7.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters do not have the benefit of the official translation either on the screen or in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the best thing is to put it on the ELMO as well if we have -- you don't have a hard copy ... not even the Prosecution? Mr. Thayer, do you have the hard copy of this document in English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Did we find a hard copy or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: One's coming, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. In the meantime, interpreters I think will have to bear with us and try to do their best. We are trying to gauge ourselves and try to find out a solution because this will happen again and again and we want to make your life much simpler. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could turn to the last page of each version, and that would be page 20 of the English and page 10 of the B/C/S, please. And if we could just scroll down. Do you see your signature, sir, your line -- your name there, where it says "drafted by"?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can we agree that this corps order flowed from the directive 7, P5 which we've spoken a lot about during your testimony, which was sent to the corps from the Main Staff just a little earlier in March? Can we agree on that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would like to clarify something.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Krstic was in charge of the drafting of this document, of this order. This term, draft, concerns the technical side of the matter, which means that the typist typed my name just because it was under the rules. I was the technical person who collected all the inputs and formulated the order to give it its present form. When the order was drafted, what I did was crafting the scheme of the decision onto the map. So I was not involved in dealing with the issues contained in the order. I believe that Krstic used both directives and other documents that wouldn't normally be used when drafting this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. You just mentioned that you believe that General Krstic used some documents that weren't normally used. Could you tell the Trial Chamber what you recall those documents were?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those would be directives 7 and 7/1 which he mentioned at the beginning of this order as the source from which he drew information to formulate the contents of this order. Everything else is just an established form that the career officers are familiar with and they can use it very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like if the witness could be shown the text of this document, whole text of this document, to see a date because I believe he speaks about another document in this case. He didn't see the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I wouldn't know the answer to that. Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Yes, Mr. Thayer, what's your comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we can certainly show the first page of the document. Again the date is right at the top, it's 20 March of 1995, and I think he would agree that was just a couple weeks after the directive 7 was issued by the Main Staff to the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me just follow-up on the comment you made about directive 7 and 7/1 would not normally have been used by General Krstic to draft such an order for combat operations as the one we're looking at now. Wouldn't those two documents or at least directive 7 been precisely the kind of document that the Drina Corps command would have relied upon in implementing the intent of the Supreme Command as communicated by the Main Staff through this directive 7?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is good that Mr. Zivanovic intervened and said that it was a different document, not the one that I meant. This is a different document and this document was drafted in the month of March when Krstic was not there, which means that this is a different document, and if you wish we can talk about this document. Obviously I was in the operations and training sector and I stood in for Colonel Krstic and I was in charge of formulating this task. Obviously I did not have an insight into these directives and that's why I did not mention them at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Thayer. Mr. Lazic, a while ago you mentioned -- you said that General Krstic mentioned directive 7 and 7/1 as the source of this at the beginning of this order. Could you show me the passage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is precisely what I've just explained. I meant that the order concerns Srebrenica, but this is a different order which was drafted much earlier with regard to Srebrenica. In the order about Srebrenica, Krstic relied on directive 7 and 7/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir, let's see if we can agree on a couple of things. You recall being shown P5 a number of times by my friends and the date of directive 7 was March 8th, and that was transited to the corps on or about March 17th. Is that correct? Do you recall that? I can show you the document if you want to see it.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you don't have to show it to me. I agree with you, with your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, this document that we have on the screen, 65 ter 203, which is titled: "Order for defence and active combat operations operative number 7," my question to you, sir, is: Doesn't this follow from the Main Staff's directive 7 which was received by the corps, according to your testimony sometime in March of 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazic, before you answer. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I believe that it would be fair to show to the witness whole document. He has opportunity just to see a few lines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazic, can you answer the question? Do you need the document? Can you answer the question without the document or do you prefer to have the document in front of you? In any case we can provide you with it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can explain. This number 7 is obviously in -- may be associated with a directive but it has nothing to do whatsoever with the directive. Here number 7 is -- just shows the sequence of orders that the corps issued. So this operative number 7 has nothing whatsoever to do with directive number 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We've got a slightly different but related point. We are unhappy with the formulation of my learned friend Mr. Thayer's last question when he calls it Main Staff's directive 7. The terminology in this regard is very important. Could he be careful, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Josse, for that. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you need to look at the whole document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, but I think we need to make this clear. Is it Main Staff directive number 7 or is it someone else's?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I think it's fair to refer to it as a Main Staff document or a Supreme Command document, we've heard testimony about the participation in the Main Staff, by the Main Staff, it's transited by the Main Staff to the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We of course say it's the Supreme Command document. That's the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And indeed it is. Let's proceed. Mr. Lazic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you need to look at this entire document before we proceed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have to look at it unless you want to point me to specific parts of it and question me about those parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, that's certainly what we're going to do, sir. So if you would like to look at it before we do that, please feel free to do so, otherwise I'll take you to the various portions.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Start with the specific portions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What I want to do first, sir, is look at some of the more technical aspects of this order. I think you testified that one thing you did participate in was the more technical aspects of this document. Now, the directive 7 that flowed to the corps tasked the corps to plan several operations and this order that you drafted refers to a few of them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, one of those operations was Spreca 95. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That was mentioned in the directive 7 that the Drina Corps received, and it's mentioned again in this document. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if I recall, Spreca 95 was to take place in a location to the north/north-west of Zvornik. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That operation's focus was to be in the area of East Bosnia Corps and overlaps with parts of the Drina Corps, i.e., the north-western part of the area of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that information that you just provided is contained in both the directive that -- the directive 7 that came to the corps and in this document that you drafted. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall that Spreca 95 was actually begun -- was planned and begun in the spring of 1995. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have a vague recollection of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll get to some more Spreca documents a little bit later. Now, according to this order that you drafted, sir, Spreca 95 was to be followed by an operation to liberate Gorazde and to reduce Gorazde to its urban area. Do you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, very vaguely. I do remember but not very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And according to this document, and we're looking at page 6 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S if we want to follow along, that operation name was to be Zvijezde, if I'm pronouncing it all correctly, sir, does that ring any bells with you? If you want to look at page 3 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is about a special operation, a different operation, that was supposed to be carried out in cooperation with the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and the Herzegovina Corps. Zvijezde 95 got its name after the mountain bearing the same name, I believe -- I'm sure of that. Mostly when deciding on the names of these operations, the nearest features, geographical features, would be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that Gorazde operation was to be followed by a strategic operation under the leadership of the Main Staff and you will recall that this was found in the directive that flowed to you, directive 7 to the corps, that strategic operation was to be called Prozor 95. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall the details of the contents, but I suppose I can agree with you and say that that probably was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you described a little bit about what your involvement was in drafting this document. Could you be a little bit more specific. What was your role as chief of operations and training at the Drina Corps command in drafting in document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most probably I was in charge of drafting the document, which means I had collected input from the organs who were duty-bound to provide their respective inputs for the contents of the order. Since the commander Zivanovic was at the command, I suppose that he was the one who authored item 4 entitled: "Decision." I did not author the item myself, and also item 5 which referred to the tasks of the subordinated units, it was the commander's task to draft those items. My task was to technically formulate and word the order, to shape it in the way it was supposed to be shaped, and to complete it the way it was supposed to be completed. That was my task.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, having discussed a little bit and taken a look at the document in some more detail and having seen these operations which are described here which were specifically referred to in the directive 7 that flowed to you at the Drina Corps, can we agree that this document in fact flowed from directive 7?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious that this item was drafted by the corps commander because he was privy to directive number 7 of the Supreme Command of the armed forces of Republika Srpska, and he had used the opportunity to inform all those who were the recipients of this order to inform them about the long-term tasks of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, sir, what you're saying is that this document that you helped draft at the Drina Corps level was used by your commander to inform the corps about the overall strategic objectives that were included, encapsulated, described in the directive 7 from the Supreme Command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the corps, but the corps commanders who were the recipients of this order, to whom this order was sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, I'm not sure I understand your answer, sir. Let me try again.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you allow me, I can explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order was sent to the brigade commanders. It gives you the list of addressees in the heading, and this served to inform the brigade commanders with the things that awaited Drina Corps in the forthcoming longer period. The commander had decided to do so and I don't see any other reason why all this would have been included in an order of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I think I see where the confusion lies. When I asked you a few lines ago - and I'll just repeat the question - what you're saying is that this document that you helped draft at the Drina Corps level was used by your commander to inform the corps, and when I say "the corps," I just mean the Drina Corps, I wasn't referring to informing all the other corps, to inform the corps and its subordinate commands about the overall strategic objectives that were contained in directive 7 --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the corps, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, but the witness never mentioned strategic objectives but long-term objectives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But what's the difference between strategic and long-term?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Either way, Your Honour, I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the difference?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One's strategy covers plans and the short and on the long-haul.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Because first witness testified about strategic objectives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's not waste time. Go ahead, Mr. Lazic, if you could answer the question, please, and we'll have a break in three minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Strategic goals are something else. A reference here is made to the tasks of the Drina Corps over a period of time. Once again I may have used a wrong word when I said that corps commanders should have been informed. The commander of Drina Corps could not have informed his peers, the commanders of other corps, but just his unit commanders. Maybe this order, combat order, was used to inform the subordinated commanders in the Drina Corps about the tasks and duties that await the Drina Corps in the forthcoming period. Did I make myself clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You did, sir. I think we solved the confusion, which is literally just a matter of a word. I was just referring to a single corps. Now, just to finish up on this one question. When General Krstic used this document to inform the Drina Corps and its subordinate commands of these long-term goals and objectives, he was relying on the directive 7 that he received from his superior command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that the witness said three times that this document was used to inform the commanders of subordinate units, and the Prosecutor repeats that this document was used to inform the Drina Corps and the subordinate units. I believe that this document stems from the Drina Corps, so I do not believe that this document was used to inform the people who wrote it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Fauveau. Yes, Mr. Thayer, what's your comment to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Frankly, I don't understand the objection, Your Honour. I think he's made it clear. I think we've solved whatever confusion there was, so I don't understand that objection. I think it's clear now on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's have the break now, 25 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, I am informed that the next witness is already here, but having heard you before state that you will approximately require about three hours, that means that you won't finish this witness today or even if you do, there is no point in keeping the witness, the other witness, here, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. I had informed my friend that that would be the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. No, no, because I don't wish to keep him waiting here in vain. So do you agree to that, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but I am not aware that he was brought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He is. So, Madam Registrar, if you could arrange for his transportation, please. Thank you. Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Colonel, good morning again. I just want to clarify some of the confusion that we left at the break. Now -- and I've spoken with my learned friend from the Miletic team to hopefully clarify some of the confusion which is literally a matter of translations and word usage. Looking at this document, the Drina Corps order number 7, when General Zivanovic - and I think I may have misspoken before when I said General Krstic - but when General Zivanovic used this document to inform the Drina Corps's subordinate commands, that is, its brigades of these long-term goals and objectives he was relying on the directive 7 that he received from his superior command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He received it from the Supreme Command through his superior command. It was a Supreme Command directive which he received through his superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, he was communicating to the Drina Corps brigades those long-term objectives and goals contained in his superior command's directive 7. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, at this time you testified that General Krstic was absent. Can you tell the Trial Chamber why he was absent?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it is known that Krstic had a misfortune to have lost his leg. I think it was before the 1st of January, 1995, and that that is why he was absent, because he was being treated.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in relation to that I'd like to show you 65 ter 3329, if we could. Take a moment, please, sir, and read the document. Let me know when you feel comfortable talking about it.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So this document which is dated March 20th of 1995, the same date in fact as the last document we looked at, this is formally appointing you standing in for General Krstic, the Chief of Staff of the Drina Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, as chief of operations and training you were always simultaneously deputy Chief of Staff; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So can you tell the Trial Chamber how being appointed standing in for the Chief of Staff affects your duties and responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it increased the burden and the type of engagement at work; however, that should not present a hindrance concerning my original duty, this being the head of the operations and training organ. Part of the job of the Chief of Staff was taken over by the corps commander as well. As for the rest of the duties pertaining to Chief of Staff, I did the rest as much as I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And presumably, sir, with the absence of General Krstic during this period of time, General Zivanovic relied upon you more often in connection with your standing position as well as your standing-in position. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to 65 ter 203, if we could, please. And this is the Drina Corps order number 7 that we were looking at before. Now, it was you who coordinated all of the various organs, collected their input and drafted the document that we're looking at now; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And it was you who assessed it, evaluated it, prior to submitting it to your commander in terms of determining whether it made sense as an order. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had the time to go through it in detail, then that may have been the case; but one definitely needs to go through everything to see whether all the items are in order as specified by the rules. Then if there's any time left, you turn to the contents. I don't know, though, whether I had studied this in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, let's talk about the Supreme Command's directive 7. That came to the corps just prior to this document being drafted. When the Main Staff was assisting the Supreme Command in drafting directive 7, sir, who in the Drina Corps was consulted in order to draft the Drina Corps's tasks in the Supreme Command's directive 7?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such a practice in place that when the Main Staff were drafting a directive to consult their subordinate units. I'm not familiar with such practice. I suppose no one of the Drina Corps participated in the assistance when directive number 7 was being drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So it's your testimony, sir, that it was entirely the Main Staff that would have used its resources in determining what the various corps assignments, duties, responsibilities were to be in this long-term document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe the corps commanders had some sort of cooperation with the Main Staff. I don't know about it, though, because I couldn't know what they were doing at that level of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, this document 203 that we're looking at, sir, if we look at page 8 of the English, and that's page 4 of the B/C/S, there's a reference definitively liberating the Drina Valley region. Now, my question to you, sir, is yesterday you testified that the Krivaja 95 operation - and this was at page 21 of yesterday's transcript - was the first attempt to carry out any kind of action in relation to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that level and with such tasks and goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, liberating the Srebrenica and the upper and middle Podrinje regions had been an objective of the Bosnian Serb government and military for more than two years prior to you drafting this document on March 20th, 1995, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And liberating the region meant forcing the Muslim population out of those areas; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operation wasn't planned quite that way. If one looks at the order to carry out that task, one can see that the goal was not to force the Muslim population to move. The goal was to separate the enclaves. As to what the operation subsequently turned into, I wouldn't know since I didn't participate in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, sir, we'll get to the combat order Krivaja 95 in due time, but what I want to focus your attention on now is the political and military leadership's focus for some time, for over two years, on forcing the Muslim population out of the areas that included Srebrenica, the upper and middle Podrinje region. Now, you served in the Main Staff headquarters as assistant chief of the operations department from June of 1992 through May of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I think you've testified that when you were there it was understaffed. Do I have that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe how that lack of officers affected your duties and responsibilities when you were at the Main Staff in the operations department?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those organs that existed within the Main Staff were fully engaged trying to meet all of their tasks. That meant that longer working hours had to be put in and the hours would have been less had they been staffed 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you find that staff officers like yourself also on occasions had greater responsibility than you might otherwise have had because of the poor staffing situation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not the case since due attention was paid to the principles in place. The commander and the Chief of Staff were those in command and there was no chance of anyone else being involved in that area of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, sir. I'm not referring to anybody jumping command. I'm simply referring to within your specialty sector, did you find yourself or did your colleagues find yourselves having to undertake more responsibility as a result of the lack of staffing? That's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One couldn't put it that way, greater responsibility. I would only say more work.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, are you familiar, sir, with directive for further operations of the VRS, directive operational number 4?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall it superficially. I may be able to recall some of the content, although it wasn't made available to me just like any other directives. I could only learn from the Chief of Staff what some parts of the directives contained.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, let's go to directive 4. This is 65 ter 29, please. Sir, you testified yesterday about your knowledge and your experience and your familiarity with directives, both from the Supreme Command and from the Main Staff. Can you describe for the Trial Chamber what role you and your department played in drafting directive 4. And if you need some time to take a look at the document, sir, please do so and I can provide you with a hard copy if you need it.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please scroll down a bit faster so that I can go through the document more quickly. Go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have to say it is better to show the witness hard copy of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's available.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: As I said, I've got a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Usher, if you could assist, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While he's reading, Mr. Thayer, I refer to your question which appears on page 34, from line 19 to line 25, do you follow?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 34, line 19 to 25. Although the witness answered yes, but he didn't -- I think he didn't answer the first part of your question so you're going to pursue that part further?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That is what I am precisely doing now, and I -- I understood his answer to be to the second part of the question, not to the first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wanted to make sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And just for the record I think he did answer it immediately prior to that. He answered that specific question and I don't think my learned friend was pleased with the answer. He added it and then asked another question, but immediately prior to that I think the witness does answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's proceed and let's wait for Mr. Thayer's next question and we see how it goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, let's go to page 5 of the directive in English, and that's page 11, Colonel, of the B/C/S. I think you'll find it at the top of the page. This is subheading D of paragraph 4. I've highlighted the section for you and there's a blue tab there, sir. Do you have that? I'll just read out the assignment for the Drina Corps. "From its present positions, its main forces shall persistently defend Visegrad, the dam, Zvornik and the corridor while the rest of its forces in the wider Podrinje region shall exhaust the enemy, inflict the heaviest possible losses on him, and force him to leave the Birac, Zepa, and Gorazde areas together with the Muslim population." When you were at the Main Staff, sir, do you recall that assignment being given to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall it because this directive was done by the Chief of Staff and forwarded it directly to the corps commanders. At the time I wasn't familiar with any details contained in the directive.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall what efforts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just one moment. Madam Fauveau, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think it would be equitable for the witness to be shown the complete paragraph to read it for the record or at least leave him the time to read, give him this part of paragraph without the following part. It may be in a way -- the real meaning of the paragraph may appear as different if it's not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, this witness had an opportunity to review the document. I'd like to continue my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so. I think this was out of place. Let's proceed. Thank you. In the meantime, Mr. Ostojic and Mr. Nikolic, we've just been informed that the registrar has handed down its decision replacing Mr. Meek as co-counsel by Mr. Predrag Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you recall what efforts the Drina Corps took pursuant to directive 7 to liberate the Podrinje region? I'm sorry, I misspoke, that's directive 4 we're looking at, not directive 7. Do you recall what efforts the Drina Corps undertook pursuant to directive 4 to move out the Muslim population, liberate that region?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the Drina Corps did not have the necessary forces and ability to deal with these tasks. I believe the tasks were postponed until 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's look at a couple of documents, sir. If we could be shown 3029, please. Do you see the document in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, this is a 24 November 1992 Drina Corps command order to the Zvornik Brigade, and I note for the record there's a typo in the English version in the very first portion where it refers to a confidential number 02/3. If we look at the original B/C/S, it should be 02/5. And, sir, you would agree with me, if you want to look at directive 4 there, that this reference to 02/5 is a reference in fact to directive 4. Is that correct? It refers to it by both order number and the date.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My question is simple, sir. Does this document in its opening language refer to directive 4 by its order number and the date, 02/5, 19 November 1992? And I'd invite you to look at the hard copy I gave you of directive 4 if you want to verify that.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious that the contents of item 1, one would say, stem out of the directive.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, let's look at paragraph 1, sir. "Launch an attack using the main body of troops and major equipment to inflict on the enemy the highest possible losses, exhaust them, break them up, or force them to surrender and force the Muslim local population to abandon the area of Cerska, Zepa, Srebrenica, and Gorazde." Do you recall this objective that we saw in directive 4 being communicated by the Drina Corps to one of its brigades, namely the Zvornik Brigade? Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall because in 1992 I was not in the Drina Corps but in the Main Staff. I must note that the person who gave this task to the Zvornik Brigade obviously did not take into account that the Zvornik Brigade could not carry out such a task because it was too big a bite to swallow for that brigade. But at that time Zvornik had been reduced to a very narrow area and the road between Zvornik and Konjevic Polje was not passable. That's why it was fully expected from the Zvornik Brigade to make it passable, to liberate that road. And this is exactly what can be read in the rest of paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And so, sir, can you explain to the Trial Chamber how the local Muslim population being forced to abandon these areas was at all related to freeing up a road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I don't know how the author of this order could have outlined such radical objectives for this brigade. The sentence is -- has -- was obviously copied or had been received from somebody. In my view, this task should not have been given to any brigade because it's too big. In any case, this brigade had nothing whatsoever to do with Srebrenica, Gorazde, or Zepa for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll look at some more documents along those lines, sir. In the meantime let's turn to page 2 of the English, and this is on page 3 of the B/C/S which you'll see soon on the screen. And we're looking at paragraph -- subparagraph (c) under moral and psychological preparations. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: "Before initiating any kind of operation, inform the unit members about the important aim of that operation and underline that the outcome of minor actions and of the whole operation is of a crucial importance to the realization of the aim of the Serbian people, namely, the creation and establishment of the Serbian state in these areas."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I notice that the accused Miletic is standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. General Miletic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED MILETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't understand why the Defence counsel don't react. The person, the witness was not in the Drina Corps, he did not author the order, he can't say anything about it, and the Prosecutor is putting in questions about something that he is not in a position to talk about. They should call somebody else who would be better suited to answer questions on this particular and similar types of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: With the advice, Your Honour, if I may move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have no comments on that. Please move ahead, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, my first question is: The section that you just read under morale, when you were at the Main Staff did you understand that to be an objective of the VRS, that is, the creation and establishment of a Serbian state in those areas? When you were at the Main Staff, did you understand that to be an objective?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My personal view, you mean, about the creation of a Serbian state in that area, well, I personally --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Let me ask you first. My question was: Did you understand that to be an objective of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I think that it was, that this was to say that even the minor operations should be carried out successfully in order to liberate the areas where the Serbian population lived and in view of the situation as it was in 1992 to separate the peoples in Bosnia and Herzegovina on ethnic grounds. In view of all of that, this could have been a logical objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: My question to you, sir, was: Was that an objective based on your experience in the Main Staff, the separation of people along ethnic lines? Was that an objective of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before you answer that question. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the witness already answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm following up on an answer which was, in view of all that this could have been a logical objective. I'm asking again whether it was an objective, based on the witness's experience in the Main Staff, to ethnically separate the peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, we are fine with the question. Please -- I see you standing, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, I would like to join the objection. I just note on page 42, line 12, I think the witness does answer it. He first says "I think so." Then he proceeds to say "I think that it was," so I think the objection, with all due respect, even though the Court overruled, it has been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think Mr. Ostojic may be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the problem is at the end of that answer he says: "In view of all of that, this could have been a logical objective," and that's why I'm following up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, go ahead. Mr. Lazic, if you could answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I simply can share with you my feelings in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't talk on behalf of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Colonel, I'm not asking you to be a spokesman for the VRS. What I'm asking you is, based on your experience at the Main Staff in operations and training, based on the orders you saw coming in and going out, was an objective of the VRS to separate the peoples of Bosnia and Herzegovina by their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the main objective of the VRS was to defend the Serb population from the attacks coming from the other side, and if there was no other solution available, then to separate all of us on ethnic principles. And I believe that that was the understanding of every individual member of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. General Gvero.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED GVERO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, item (c) mentions the creation of a state of the Serbian people, but it doesn't mention the national separation of the peoples. Second of all, there is no single state in the world inhabited by members of only one people. In other words, the creation of the state of the Serb people does not imply the separation of peoples along the ethnic lines. This is a document of the Drina Corps and not of the Main Staff. This was worded and formulated in the Drina Corps. That would be my last remark and I thank you for you giving me the opportunity to voice it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, General Gvero. Yes, Mr. Thayer. One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Thayer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall that over the next few months following the issuance of directive 4 from the Main Staff to the corps and in relation to the Drina Corps order that you just saw, do you recall that the VRS executed a campaign to force the local Muslim population out of the areas in the Podrinje, including Cerska, Konjevic Polje, Kamenica, and Srebrenica? Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that there was any pressure put on the population, but there were actions being carried out in the area and I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall that that operation was called Proboj?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: With the Chamber's indulgence, I'm actually seeing if I can cut some questions from my examination. Okay, I've reduced my examination a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, I just want to show you one document.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could see 3373, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Colonel, let me know when you've had a chance to review the document.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We have a 25 January 1993 urgent communication from General Zivanovic from the command of the Drina Corps to the command of the Uzice Corps. What was the Uzice Corps, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word is self-explanatory. It was a corps headquartered in Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where is that, please?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where geographically in Serbia in relation to the eastern enclaves or the Podrinje is Uzice? How about in relation to the Drina River, can you orient us a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is in western part of Serbia, one of the towns en route from the Drina towards central Serbia, one of the bigger settlements on that route.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If we look at the first main paragraph it says: "In order to complete the given tasks according to code Proboj as diligently as possible I report that we launched active combat operation with all available forces in order to contain as much as possible enemy forces so that you and your neighbours can successfully carry out your tasks." Now, sir, do you have any recollection as to why the Drina Corps would be communicating with a corps located in Serbia, across the river, having looked at this document and in your experience?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO LAZIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I suppose that General Zivanovic, who was colonel at the time, thought that he should inform them that on our side in the territory indicated herein, there was combat going on so as to inform the corps in Serbia what was happening in the area over here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
